1	"""Replayable commit checkpoints for offline coordination.
2	
3	A checkpoint names an ``id``, the two 64-char lowercase hex digests of the
4	state and audit bytes it binds, and the ``stage`` the commit has reached.
5	Stages advance in the fixed order::
6	
7	    prepared -> state -> audit -> committed
8	
9	Checkpoints are kept in an index stored as UTF-8 compact JSON::
10	
11	    {"items":[{"audit":...,"id":...,"stage":...,"state":...},...],"version":1}\\n
12	
13	The top-level keys are fixed in the order ``items`` then ``version`` and
14	``version`` is always the integer 1.  ``items`` is an array of records
15	sorted ascending by ``id`` (ids are unique); each record carries the str
16	keys ``audit``, ``id``, ``stage`` and ``state`` in that order.  Non-ASCII
17	characters are preserved unescaped and the file ends with exactly one
18	``\\n``.
19	
20	A missing index file stands for an empty index.  An existing file is
21	corrupt unless it is one compact UTF-8 JSON encoding of a valid index:
22	no stray whitespace or non-canonical escapes and exactly one trailing
23	``\\n``.  The object *key order* carries no meaning, however, so an
24	otherwise identical compact encoding with the top-level or record keys
25	permuted is accepted as equivalent; files written by this module always
26	use the canonical key order described above.
27	
28	A brand-new id may only be recorded at the ``prepared`` stage.  Replaying
29	the same id with identical digests at the same stage is idempotent and
30	leaves the file bytes untouched; the stage may then advance one step at a
31	time, each advance replacing the file atomically.  Changed digests, a
32	stage regression or a skipped stage are rejected and never touch the file.
33	
34	:func:`resume` drives a single recovery step.  Its request carries only
35	the ``id``, ``state`` and ``audit`` digests and ``observed`` names the
36	stage the caller believes it has reached (``None`` for a fresh resume).
37	A new id is only accepted with ``observed=None`` and starts at
38	``prepared``.  For an existing id with identical digests, ``observed``
39	of ``None`` or the current stage only queries the index (leaving the
40	file bytes untouched), while the adjacent next stage advances it once;
41	a regression, a skipped stage or an illegal value is rejected without
42	touching the file.  The return value names the next action for the
43	processed stage: ``persist_state`` after ``prepared``,
44	``append_audit`` after ``state``, ``bind_receipt`` after ``audit`` and
45	``done`` after ``committed``.
46	
47	:func:`commit` drives a whole commit to completion.  Its ``paths`` map
48	names the ``checkpoint``, ``state``, ``audit`` and ``receipt`` files and
49	its request carries the ``id``, the full merge ``state`` and one audit
50	``event``.  The state digest is the SHA-256 of the canonical state bytes
51	storage writes; the audit digest is the hash of the one appended audit
52	record.  A first commit persists the state, appends exactly one event,
53	binds a receipt for the id and both digests, and advances the checkpoint
54	through the stages in order.  Replaying the same call -- after an
55	interruption or once committed -- deterministically resumes at the
56	recorded stage and performs every remaining side effect at most once,
57	returning the same ``audit``, ``id``, ``stage`` (``committed``) and
58	``state`` dict.  A digest conflict, or a checkpoint stage whose
59	artifacts do not match it, raises :class:`ValueError` and leaves the
60	files unchanged.
61	
62	:func:`inspect` is a strictly read-only counterpart taking only the
63	``paths`` map.  A missing checkpoint index yields an empty list; every
64	existing checkpoint is reported with its ``audit``, ``id``, ``stage``
65	and ``state`` values plus a ``status`` of ``recoverable``,
66	``committed`` or ``conflict`` derived from the state bytes, the audit
67	chain and any bound receipt.  Neither :func:`inspect` nor
68	:func:`commit` ever treats an existing-but-unreadable state as a mere
69	conflict: when at least one of the main and backup state files exists
70	but neither holds a valid state, :class:`CorruptStateError` propagates.
71	"""
72

76	import json
77	import os
78	import re

92	VERSION = "version"

95	STAGE_STATE = "state"
96	STAGE_AUDIT = "audit"
97	COMMITTED = "committed"

100	_RESUME_KEYS = (ID, STATE, AUDIT)
101	_COMMIT_KEYS = (ID, STATE, "event")
102	_PATH_KEYS = ("checkpoint", STATE, AUDIT, "receipt")
103	_RECORD_KEYS = (AUDIT, ID, STAGE, STATE)
104	_INDEX_KEYS = (ITEMS, VERSION)
105	_INDEX_VERSION = 1
106	
107	_EVENT = "event"
108	_CHECKPOINT = "checkpoint"
109	_RECEIPT = "receipt"

112	_STAGE_RANK = {stage: rank for rank, stage in enumerate(_STAGES)}
113	
114	# Statuses reported by inspect for a checkpoint against its artifacts.
115	RECOVERABLE = "recoverable"

118	# Action performed once the checkpoint for a stage has been durably
119	# recorded: persist state after prepared, append the audit entry after
120	# state, bind the receipt after audit, and nothing after committed.
121	_NEXT_ACTIONS = {
122	    PREPARED: "persist_state",
123	    STAGE_STATE: "append_audit",
124	    STAGE_AUDIT: "bind_receipt",
125	    COMMITTED: "done",

133	    """The checkpoint index exists but its bytes are not a valid index."""

137	    return isinstance(value, str) and _DIGEST_RE.fullmatch(value) is not None

141	    """Validate one checkpoint request and return a fresh dict in record order."""
142	    if not isinstance(request, dict):
143	        raise TypeError("request must be a dict")
144	    if set(request.keys()) != set(_REQUEST_KEYS):
145	        raise ValueError(

154	        raise ValueError("request id must match [A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}")

156	        raise ValueError("request state must be 64 lowercase hex characters")
157	    if not _is_digest(request[AUDIT]):

165	    return {

167	        ID: checkpoint_id,
168	        STAGE: stage,
169	        STATE: request[STATE],
170	    }

173	def _validated_resume_request(request: Any) -> dict[str, str]:
174	    """Validate one resume request and return a fresh dict in record order."""
175	    if not isinstance(request, dict):
176	        raise TypeError("request must be a dict")
177	    if set(request.keys()) != set(_RESUME_KEYS):

198	def _serialize_index(records: list[dict[str, str]]) -> bytes:
199	    ordered = [
200	        {AUDIT: record[AUDIT], ID: record[ID], STAGE: record[STAGE],
201	         STATE: record[STATE]}
202	        for record in records
203	    ]
204	    index = {ITEMS: ordered, VERSION: _INDEX_VERSION}
205	    text = json.dumps(index, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":")) + "\n"
206	    return text.encode("utf-8")
207	
208	
209	def _parse_index(raw: bytes) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
210	    """Validate every byte of a checkpoint index and return its records.
211	
212	    Raises :class:`CorruptTransactionError` for any UTF-8/JSON failure,
213	    non-canonical byte encoding, wrong key set, bad version, duplicate or
214	    unsorted ids, or a field that is not a well-formed str.  The order of
215	    object keys does not matter: a compact encoding whose only difference
216	    from the canonical form is key permutation is an equivalent index.
217	    """
218	    if raw == b"":
219	        raise CorruptTransactionError("checkpoint index is empty")
220	    try:
221	        text = raw.decode("utf-8")
222	    except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:
223	        raise CorruptTransactionError("checkpoint index is not valid UTF-8") from exc
224	    try:
225	        data = json.loads(text)
226	    except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
227	        raise CorruptTransactionError("checkpoint index is not valid JSON") from exc
228	
229	    if not isinstance(data, dict):
230	        raise CorruptTransactionError("checkpoint index must be a JSON object")
231	    if set(data.keys()) != set(_INDEX_KEYS):
232	        raise CorruptTransactionError(
233	            "checkpoint index must contain exactly the keys 'items' and 'version'"
234	        )
235	    version = data[VERSION]
236	    # bool is a subclass of int; the version must be a genuine integer.
237	    if isinstance(version, bool) or not isinstance(version, int) or version != 1:
238	        raise CorruptTransactionError("checkpoint index version must be the integer 1")
239	    raw_items = data[ITEMS]
240	    if not isinstance(raw_items, list):
241	        raise CorruptTransactionError("checkpoint index items must be an array")
242	
243	    records: list[dict[str, str]] = []
244	    for position, item in enumerate(raw_items):
245	        where = f"checkpoint index item {position}"
246	        if not isinstance(item, dict):
247	            raise CorruptTransactionError(f"{where} must be a JSON object")
248	        if set(item.keys()) != set(_RECORD_KEYS):
249	            raise CorruptTransactionError(
250	                f"{where} must contain exactly the keys 'audit', 'id', 'stage' "
251	                "and 'state'"
252	            )
253	        audit_digest = item[AUDIT]
254	        record_id = item[ID]
255	        stage = item[STAGE]
256	        state_digest = item[STATE]
257	        if not isinstance(record_id, str) or _ID_RE.fullmatch(record_id) is None:
258	            raise CorruptTransactionError(f"{where} has an invalid id")
259	        if not isinstance(stage, str) or stage not in _STAGE_RANK:
260	            raise CorruptTransactionError(f"{where} has an invalid stage")
261	        if not isinstance(state_digest, str) or not _is_digest(state_digest):
262	            raise CorruptTransactionError(
263	                f"{where} state must be 64 lowercase hex characters"
264	            )
265	        if not isinstance(audit_digest, str) or not _is_digest(audit_digest):
266	            raise CorruptTransactionError(
267	                f"{where} audit must be 64 lowercase hex characters"
268	            )
269	        records.append(
270	            {AUDIT: audit_digest, ID: record_id, STAGE: stage, STATE: state_digest}
271	        )
272	
273	    ids = [record[ID] for record in records]
274	    if any(left >= right for left, right in zip(ids, ids[1:])):
275	        raise CorruptTransactionError(
276	            "checkpoint index ids must be unique and sorted ascending"
277	        )
278	
279	    # Reject stray whitespace, non-canonical escapes, duplicate keys and
280	    # any encoding that is not a single compact form of the validated
281	    # structure.  Re-serialising the parsed object while preserving its
282	    # parsed key order tolerates permuted object keys (a semantically
283	    # equivalent compact index) while still rejecting every other
284	    # byte-level deviation; writes always use the canonical key order of
285	    # _serialize_index.
286	    if not raw.endswith(b"\n") or raw.endswith(b"\n\n"):
287	        raise CorruptTransactionError(
288	            "checkpoint index must end with exactly one newline"
289	        )
290	    compact = json.dumps(data, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"))
291	    if compact != text[:-1]:
292	        raise CorruptTransactionError("checkpoint index is not canonically encoded")
293	    return records

305	def _atomic_write(path: str, payload: bytes) -> None:
306	    tmp_path = path + ".tmp"
307	    with open(tmp_path, "wb") as handle:
308	        handle.write(payload)
309	        handle.flush()
310	        os.fsync(handle.fileno())
311	    try:
312	        os.replace(tmp_path, path)
313	    except BaseException:
314	        try:
315	            os.unlink(tmp_path)
316	        except OSError:
317	            pass
318	        raise
319	    fd = os.open(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(path)), os.O_RDONLY)
320	    try:
321	        os.fsync(fd)
322	    finally:
323	        os.close(fd)

338	                f"checkpoint id {record[ID]!r} is already bound to different "
339	                "state or audit digests"
340	            )
341	        old_rank = _STAGE_RANK[existing[STAGE]]
342	        new_rank = _STAGE_RANK[record[STAGE]]
343	        if new_rank == old_rank:
344	            # Idempotent replay: no filesystem change.
345	            return records
346	        if new_rank < old_rank:
347	            raise ValueError(
348	                f"checkpoint id {record[ID]!r} cannot regress from stage "
349	                f"{existing[STAGE]!r} to {record[STAGE]!r}"
350	            )
351	        if new_rank > old_rank + 1:
352	            raise ValueError(
353	                f"checkpoint id {record[ID]!r} cannot skip from stage "
354	                f"{existing[STAGE]!r} to {record[STAGE]!r}"
355	            )
356	        updated = list(records)
357	        updated[position] = record
358	        _atomic_write(path, _serialize_index(updated))
359	        return updated
360	
361	    if record[STAGE] != PREPARED:
362	        raise ValueError("a new checkpoint id must start at the 'prepared' stage")
363	    updated = sorted(records + [record], key=lambda entry: entry[ID])
364	    _atomic_write(path, _serialize_index(updated))
365	    return updated

368	def checkpoint(
369	    path: str, request: dict[str, str] | None = None
370	) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
371	    """Record or query a replayable commit checkpoint at ``path``.
372	
373	    With ``request=None`` this is a pure query returning every checkpoint.
374	    Otherwise ``request`` must contain exactly the str keys ``id``,
375	    ``state``, ``audit`` and ``stage``: ``id`` matches
376	    ``[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}``, ``state`` and ``audit`` are 64 lowercase hex
377	    characters, and ``stage`` is one of ``prepared``, ``state``, ``audit``
378	    or ``committed``.
379	
380	    A new id is inserted at ``prepared``; an existing id with identical
381	    digests replays idempotently at the same stage or advances one adjacent
382	    stage.  Changed digests, a stage regression or a skipped stage raise
383	    :class:`ValueError` and leave the file unchanged.  In every case a
384	    brand-new list sorted ascending by ``id`` is returned, each element a
385	    fresh dict with the key order ``audit``, ``id``, ``stage``, ``state``.
386	
387	    Type violations raise :class:`TypeError`; a bad key set, field format
388	    or stage migration raises :class:`ValueError`; a corrupt index raises
389	    :class:`CorruptTransactionError`; other filesystem errors propagate as
390	    :class:`OSError`.
391	    """
392	    if not isinstance(path, str):
393	        raise TypeError("path must be a str")
394	
395	    record = _validated_request(request) if request is not None else None
396	    records = _read_index(path)
397	    if record is not None:
398	        records = _apply(path, records, record)
399	
400	    return [
401	        {
402	            AUDIT: record[AUDIT],
403	            ID: record[ID],
404	            STAGE: record[STAGE],
405	            STATE: record[STATE],
406	        }
407	        for record in records
408	    ]

411	def resume(
412	    path: str, request: dict[str, str], observed: str | None = None
413	) -> str:
414	    """Recover one commit step at ``path`` and return the next action.
415	
416	    ``request`` must contain exactly the str keys ``id``, ``state`` and
417	    ``audit`` in the same format as the matching :func:`checkpoint`
418	    fields.  ``observed`` must be ``None`` or one of the stages
419	    ``prepared``, ``state``, ``audit`` or ``committed``; it names the
420	    stage the caller has observed for the id.
421	
422	    A new id is only accepted with ``observed=None`` and is recorded at
423	    the ``prepared`` stage.  An existing id must be bound to the same
424	    ``state`` and ``audit`` digests; with ``observed=None`` or the
425	    current stage the call is a pure query and leaves the file bytes
426	    untouched, while ``observed`` naming the adjacent next stage
427	    advances the checkpoint exactly once.  A stage regression, a skipped
428	    stage or an illegal ``observed`` value raise :class:`ValueError` and
429	    leave the file unchanged.
430	
431	    The return value is the next action for the processed stage:
432	    ``persist_state`` for ``prepared``, ``append_audit`` for ``state``,
433	    ``bind_receipt`` for ``audit`` and ``done`` for ``committed``.
434	
435	    A non-str ``observed`` other than ``None`` raises :class:`TypeError`;
436	    the remaining type and value rules, :class:`CorruptTransactionError`
437	    and :class:`OSError` propagation match :func:`checkpoint`.
438	    """
439	    if not isinstance(path, str):
440	        raise TypeError("path must be a str")
441	
442	    requested = _validated_resume_request(request)
443	    if observed is not None:
444	        if not isinstance(observed, str):
445	            raise TypeError(
446	                "observed must be None or one of 'prepared', 'state', "
447	                "'audit' or 'committed'"
448	            )
449	        if observed not in _STAGE_RANK:
450	            raise ValueError(
451	                "observed must be None or one of 'prepared', 'state', "
452	                "'audit' or 'committed'"
453	            )
454	
455	    records = _read_index(path)
456	    existing = next(
457	        (record for record in records if record[ID] == requested[ID]), None
458	    )
459	
460	    if existing is None:
461	        if observed is not None:
462	            raise ValueError(
463	                f"checkpoint id {requested[ID]!r} is new and may only be "
464	                "resumed with observed=None"
465	            )
466	        record = {
467	            AUDIT: requested[AUDIT],
468	            ID: requested[ID],
469	            STAGE: PREPARED,
470	            STATE: requested[STATE],
471	        }
472	        _apply(path, records, record)
473	        return _NEXT_ACTIONS[PREPARED]
474	
475	    if (
476	        existing[STATE] != requested[STATE]
477	        or existing[AUDIT] != requested[AUDIT]
478	    ):
479	        raise ValueError(
480	            f"checkpoint id {requested[ID]!r} is already bound to different "
481	            "state or audit digests"
482	        )
483	
484	    current_stage = existing[STAGE]
485	    if observed is None or observed == current_stage:
486	        # Pure query: no filesystem change.
487	        processed_stage = current_stage
488	    else:
489	        current_rank = _STAGE_RANK[current_stage]
490	        observed_rank = _STAGE_RANK[observed]
491	        if observed_rank < current_rank:
492	            raise ValueError(
493	                f"checkpoint id {requested[ID]!r} cannot regress from stage "
494	                f"{current_stage!r} to {observed!r}"
495	            )
496	        if observed_rank > current_rank + 1:
497	            raise ValueError(
498	                f"checkpoint id {requested[ID]!r} cannot skip from stage "
499	                f"{current_stage!r} to {observed!r}"
500	            )
501	        record = {
502	            AUDIT: requested[AUDIT],
503	            ID: requested[ID],
504	            STAGE: observed,
505	            STATE: requested[STATE],
506	        }
507	        _apply(path, records, record)
508	        processed_stage = observed
509	
510	    return _NEXT_ACTIONS[processed_stage]
511

520	def _validated_paths(paths: Any) -> dict[str, str]:
521	    """Validate the ``checkpoint``/``state``/``audit``/``receipt`` path map."""
522	    if not isinstance(paths, dict):
523	        raise TypeError("paths must be a dict")
524	    if set(paths.keys()) != set(_PATH_KEYS):
525	        raise ValueError(
526	            "paths must contain exactly the keys 'checkpoint', 'state', "
527	            "'audit' and 'receipt'"
528	        )
529	    for key in _PATH_KEYS:
530	        if not isinstance(paths[key], str):
531	            raise TypeError(f"paths {key} must be a str")
532	    return {key: paths[key] for key in _PATH_KEYS}

535	def _validated_commit_inputs(
536	    paths: Any, request: Any
537	) -> tuple[dict[str, str], str, dict[str, Any], dict[str, str], bytes]:
538	    """Validate ``paths`` and a commit ``request`` before any file access.
539	
540	    Returns the path map, id, the caller's state, a fresh validated event
541	    dict and the canonical state bytes.  The state is checked against the
542	    merge state contract and the event against the audit event contract,
543	    so their type/value errors propagate unchanged in kind.
544	    """
545	    path_map = _validated_paths(paths)
546	    if not isinstance(request, dict):
547	        raise TypeError("request must be a dict")
548	    if set(request.keys()) != set(_COMMIT_KEYS):
549	        raise ValueError(
550	            "request must contain exactly the keys 'id', 'state' and 'event'"
551	        )
552	    checkpoint_id = request[ID]
553	    if not isinstance(checkpoint_id, str):
554	        raise TypeError("request id must be a str")
555	    if _ID_RE.fullmatch(checkpoint_id) is None:
556	        raise ValueError("request id must match [A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}")
557	
558	    payload = _state_payload(request[STATE])
559	    event = _audit._validated_event(request[_EVENT])
560	
561	    return path_map, checkpoint_id, request[STATE], event, payload

564	def _planned_audit_digest(
565	    audit_records: list[dict[str, Any]], event: dict[str, str]
566	) -> str:
567	    """Hash the audit record the next :func:`audit.append` would write.
568	
569	    Deterministic from the log's current tail: its seq is one past the
570	    last record and its prev is the last record's hash (or the zero hash
571	    for an empty log).
572	    """
573	    seq = len(audit_records) + 1
574	    prev = audit_records[-1][_audit.HASH] if audit_records else _audit._ZERO_HASH
575	    without_hash = {
576	        _audit.DETAIL: event[_audit.DETAIL],
577	        _audit.KIND: event[_audit.KIND],
578	        _audit.PREV: prev,
579	        _audit.SEQ: seq,
580	        _audit.SOURCE: event[_audit.SOURCE],
581	    }
582	    return _audit._record_hash(without_hash)

588	        and record[_audit.KIND] == event[_audit.KIND]
589	        and record[_audit.DETAIL] == event[_audit.DETAIL]
590	    )

648	    backup files exists but neither holds a valid state,

659	def _inspect_status(
660	    stage: str,
661	    state_matches: bool,
662	    audit_ok: bool,
663	    receipt: dict[str, str] | None,
664	    state_digest: str,
665	    audit_digest: str,
666	) -> str:
667	    """Classify one checkpoint from its stage and the S/A/R0/R1 facts.
668	
669	    ``S`` is ``state_matches`` (the main state file's canonical bytes hash
670	    to the state digest), ``A`` is ``audit_ok`` (a valid audit chain
671	    carries the audit digest), ``R0`` means no receipt is bound under the
672	    id and ``R1`` means that receipt binds exactly both digests.
673	    ``prepared`` with ``not A and R0``, ``state`` with ``S and R0`` and
674	    ``audit`` with ``S and A and (R0 or R1)`` are recoverable;
675	    ``committed`` with ``S and A and R1`` is committed; everything else
676	    is a conflict.
677	    """
678	    r0 = receipt is None
679	    r1 = (
680	        receipt is not None
681	        and receipt[STATE] == state_digest
682	        and receipt[AUDIT] == audit_digest
683	    )
684	    if stage == PREPARED:
685	        if not audit_ok and r0:
686	            return RECOVERABLE
687	    elif stage == STAGE_STATE:
688	        if state_matches and r0:
689	            return RECOVERABLE
690	    elif stage == STAGE_AUDIT:
691	        if state_matches and audit_ok and (r0 or r1):
692	            return RECOVERABLE
693	    else:  # COMMITTED
694	        if state_matches and audit_ok and r1:
695	            return COMMITTED
696	    return CONFLICT

699	def inspect(paths: dict[str, str]) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
700	    """Read-only inspection of every checkpoint against its bound artifacts.
701	
702	    ``paths`` must contain exactly the str keys ``checkpoint``, ``state``,
703	    ``audit`` and ``receipt``, naming the checkpoint index, the main state
704	    file (its ``path + ".bak"`` backup is consulted for corruption
705	    detection, exactly as :func:`storage.load_state` does), the audit log
706	    and the receipt index.
707	
708	    A missing checkpoint index yields ``[]`` (no other artifact is read in
709	    that case).  Otherwise one fresh dict per checkpoint is returned sorted
710	    ascending by ``id`` with the fixed key order ``audit``, ``id``,
711	    ``stage``, ``state``, ``status``; the first four values are copied from
712	    the checkpoint and ``status`` is one of ``recoverable``, ``committed``
713	    or ``conflict``.
714	
715	    Let ``S`` mean the main state file holds a complete valid state whose
716	    canonical bytes hash to the state digest, ``A`` mean a valid audit
717	    chain contains a record whose hash is the audit digest, ``R0`` mean no
718	    receipt is bound under the id and ``R1`` mean that receipt binds
719	    exactly both digests.  A ``prepared`` checkpoint with ``not A and R0``,
720	    a ``state`` checkpoint with ``S and R0`` and an ``audit`` checkpoint
721	    with ``S and A and (R0 or R1)`` are ``recoverable``; a ``committed``
722	    checkpoint with ``S and A and R1`` is ``committed``; every other
723	    combination is ``conflict``.
724	
725	    No file is created or modified.  Type violations raise
726	    :class:`TypeError` and a bad path key set raises :class:`ValueError`;
727	    when at least one of the state main/backup files exists but neither
728	    holds a valid state, :class:`CorruptStateError` propagates unchanged,
729	    as do :class:`CorruptAuditError`, :class:`CorruptReceiptError`,
730	    :class:`CorruptTransactionError` and :class:`OSError`.
731	    """
732	    path_map = _validated_paths(paths)
733	
734	    records = _read_index(path_map[_CHECKPOINT])
735	    if not records:
736	        return []
737	
738	    audit_records = _audit._read_all_records(path_map[AUDIT])
739	    receipts_by_id = {
740	        receipt[ID]: receipt for receipt in _receipt._read_index(path_map[_RECEIPT])
741	    }
742	    main_state_bytes = _main_state_canonical_bytes(path_map[STATE])
743	    _assert_state_loadable(path_map[STATE])
744	
745	    audit_hashes = {record[_audit.HASH] for record in audit_records}
746	
747	    items: list[dict[str, str]] = []
748	    for record in records:
749	        state_digest = record[STATE]
750	        audit_digest = record[AUDIT]
751	        state_matches = (
752	            main_state_bytes is not None
753	            and hashlib.sha256(main_state_bytes).hexdigest() == state_digest
754	        )
755	        audit_ok = audit_digest in audit_hashes
756	        receipt = receipts_by_id.get(record[ID])
757	        status = _inspect_status(
758	            record[STAGE], state_matches, audit_ok, receipt,
759	            state_digest, audit_digest,
760	        )
761	        items.append(
762	            {
763	                AUDIT: audit_digest,
764	                ID: record[ID],
765	                STAGE: record[STAGE],
766	                STATE: state_digest,
767	                STATUS: status,
768	            }
769	        )
770	    return items

773	def commit(paths: dict[str, str], request: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, str]:
774	    """Run one replayable commit across storage, audit, receipt and checkpoint.
775	
776	    ``paths`` must contain exactly the str keys ``checkpoint``, ``state``,
777	    ``audit`` and ``receipt``.  ``request`` must contain exactly the keys
778	    ``id`` (same format as :func:`checkpoint`), ``state`` (a state obeying
779	    the :mod:`~offline_coordination.merge` state contract) and ``event``
780	    (an event obeying the :mod:`~offline_coordination.audit` event
781	    contract).
782	
783	    The state digest is the lowercase-hex SHA-256 of the complete
784	    canonical state bytes (including the trailing ``\\n``) that
785	    :mod:`~offline_coordination.storage` persists; the audit digest is
786	    the hash of the single audit record appended for this commit.  A
787	    first commit saves the state, appends exactly one audit event, binds
788	    a receipt carrying the id and both digests, and advances the
789	    checkpoint through ``prepared``, ``state``, ``audit`` and
790	    ``committed`` in that order.
791	
792	    Replaying the same arguments -- or re-entering after an interruption
793	    -- resumes at the recorded stage and performs each remaining side
794	    effect at most once, so the result is identical and no effect is
795	    duplicated.  Every artifact is reconciled against the checkpoint
796	    stage before any file is touched: a digest conflict, or a stage
797	    whose state file, audit record or receipt is missing, extra or
798	    mismatched, raises :class:`ValueError` and leaves the files
799	    unchanged.
800	
801	    On success a brand-new dict is returned with the key order
802	    ``audit``, ``id``, ``stage``, ``state`` and ``stage`` equal to
803	    ``committed``.  Type violations raise :class:`TypeError`; bad key
804	    sets, formats, state/event values, digest conflicts and stage/
805	    artifact mismatches raise :class:`ValueError`;
806	    :class:`CorruptStateError`, :class:`CorruptAuditError`,
807	    :class:`CorruptReceiptError`, :class:`CorruptTransactionError` and
808	    :class:`OSError` propagate unchanged.
809	    """
810	    (
811	        path_map,
812	        checkpoint_id,
813	        state,
814	        event,
815	        payload,
816	    ) = _validated_commit_inputs(paths, request)
817	    checkpoint_path = path_map[_CHECKPOINT]
818	    state_path = path_map[STATE]
819	    audit_path = path_map[AUDIT]
820	    receipt_path = path_map[_RECEIPT]
821	
822	    state_digest = hashlib.sha256(payload).hexdigest()
823	
824	    # Read every artifact up front.  All reconciliation below happens
825	    # before any mutation, so a rejected commit changes nothing.
826	    audit_records = _audit._read_all_records(audit_path)
827	    planned_audit_digest = _planned_audit_digest(audit_records, event)
828	    bound_receipt = _receipt.get(receipt_path, checkpoint_id)
829	    records = _read_index(checkpoint_path)
830	    existing = next(
831	        (record for record in records if record[ID] == checkpoint_id), None
832	    )
833	    state_on_disk = _read_state_bytes(state_path)
834	    # When a state file exists but neither the main file nor the backup
835	    # holds a valid state the situation is unrecoverable, not a digest
836	    # conflict: CorruptStateError propagates before any reconciliation.
837	    _assert_state_loadable(state_path)
838	
839	    need_save = False
840	    need_append = False
841	    need_receipt = False
842	
843	    if existing is None:
844	        # An id absent from the checkpoint index cannot have produced any
845	        # artifact of its own yet; a receipt bound under it is a conflict.
846	        if bound_receipt is not None:
847	            raise ValueError(
848	                f"receipt id {checkpoint_id!r} is already bound but no "
849	                "checkpoint exists for it"
850	            )
851	        audit_digest = planned_audit_digest
852	        stage = PREPARED
853	        # The state save is the first artifact effect; it is pending
854	        # unless the main file already holds the committed bytes.
855	        need_save = state_on_disk != payload
856	        need_append = True
857	        need_receipt = True
858	    else:
859	        if existing[STATE] != state_digest:
860	            raise ValueError(
861	                f"checkpoint id {checkpoint_id!r} is already bound to a "
862	                "different state digest"
863	            )
864	        audit_digest = existing[AUDIT]
865	        stage = existing[STAGE]
866	        audit_record = next(
867	            (item for item in audit_records
868	             if item[_audit.HASH] == audit_digest),
869	            None,
870	        )
871	
872	        if stage == PREPARED:
873	            # The event has not been appended yet, so its record hash must
874	            # still be derivable from the current log tail.
875	            if audit_digest != planned_audit_digest:
876	                raise ValueError(
877	                    f"checkpoint id {checkpoint_id!r} is already bound to a "
878	                    "different audit digest"
879	                )
880	            if audit_record is not None:
881	                raise ValueError(
882	                    f"checkpoint id {checkpoint_id!r} is at stage 'prepared' "
883	                    "but its audit record is already present"
884	                )
885	            if bound_receipt is not None:
886	                raise ValueError(
887	                    f"checkpoint id {checkpoint_id!r} is at stage 'prepared' "
888	                    "but a receipt is already bound"
889	                )
890	            # The save is pending unless the main file already holds the
891	            # committed bytes; save_state itself rotates any prior state.
892	            need_save = state_on_disk != payload
893	            need_append = True
894	            need_receipt = True
895	        elif stage == STAGE_STATE:
896	            if state_on_disk != payload:
897	                raise ValueError(
898	                    f"checkpoint id {checkpoint_id!r} is past stage "
899	                    "'prepared' but its state file is missing or mismatched"
900	                )
901	            if bound_receipt is not None:
902	                raise ValueError(
903	                    f"checkpoint id {checkpoint_id!r} is at stage 'state' but "
904	                    "a receipt is already bound"
905	                )
906	            if audit_record is None:
907	                # The append may still be pending; the log tail must still
908	                # derive the bound record for this event.
909	                if audit_digest != planned_audit_digest:
910	                    raise ValueError(
911	                        f"checkpoint id {checkpoint_id!r} is at stage 'state' "
912	                        "but its audit record is missing"
913	                    )
914	                need_append = True
915	            elif not _event_matches(audit_record, event):

"""Replayable commit checkpoints for offline coordination.

A checkpoint names an ``id``, the two 64-char lowercase hex digests of the
state and audit bytes it binds, and the ``stage`` the commit has reached.
Stages advance in the fixed order::

    prepared -> state -> audit -> committed

Checkpoints are kept in an index stored as UTF-8 compact JSON::

    {"items":[{"audit":...,"id":...,"stage":...,"state":...},...],"version":1}\\n

The top-level keys are fixed in the order ``items`` then ``version`` and
``version`` is always the integer 1.  ``items`` is an array of records
sorted ascending by ``id`` (ids are unique); each record carries the str
keys ``audit``, ``id``, ``stage`` and ``state`` in that order.  Non-ASCII
characters are preserved unescaped and the file ends with exactly one
``\\n``.

A missing index file stands for an empty index.  An existing file is
corrupt unless it is one compact UTF-8 JSON encoding of a valid index:
no stray whitespace or non-canonical escapes and exactly one trailing
``\\n``.  The object *key order* carries no meaning, however, so an
otherwise identical compact encoding with the top-level or record keys
permuted is accepted as equivalent; files written by this module always
use the canonical key order described above.

A brand-new id may only be recorded at the ``prepared`` stage.  Replaying
the same id with identical digests at the same stage is idempotent and
leaves the file bytes untouched; the stage may then advance one step at a
time, each advance replacing the file atomically.  Changed digests, a
stage regression or a skipped stage are rejected and never touch the file.

:func:`resume` drives a single recovery step.  Its request carries only
the ``id``, ``state`` and ``audit`` digests and ``observed`` names the
stage the caller believes it has reached (``None`` for a fresh resume).
A new id is only accepted with ``observed=None`` and starts at
``prepared``.  For an existing id with identical digests, ``observed``
of ``None`` or the current stage only queries the index (leaving the
file bytes untouched), while the adjacent next stage advances it once;
a regression, a skipped stage or an illegal value is rejected without
touching the file.  The return value names the next action for the
processed stage: ``persist_state`` after ``prepared``,
``append_audit`` after ``state``, ``bind_receipt`` after ``audit`` and
``done`` after ``committed``.

:func:`commit` drives a whole commit to completion.  Its ``paths`` map
names the ``checkpoint``, ``state``, ``audit`` and ``receipt`` files and
its request carries the ``id``, the full merge ``state`` and one audit
``event``.  The state digest is the SHA-256 of the canonical state bytes
storage writes; the audit digest is the hash of the one appended audit
record.  A first commit persists the state, appends exactly one event,
binds a receipt for the id and both digests, and advances the checkpoint
through the stages in order.  Replaying the same call -- after an
interruption or once committed -- deterministically resumes at the
recorded stage and performs every remaining side effect at most once,
returning the same ``audit``, ``id``, ``stage`` (``committed``) and
``state`` dict.  A digest conflict, or a checkpoint stage whose
artifacts do not match it, raises :class:`ValueError` and leaves the
files unchanged.

:func:`inspect` is a strictly read-only counterpart taking only the
``paths`` map.  A missing checkpoint index yields an empty list; every
existing checkpoint is reported with its ``audit``, ``id``, ``stage``
and ``state`` values plus a ``status`` of ``recoverable``,
``committed`` or ``conflict`` derived from the state bytes, the audit
chain and any bound receipt.  Neither :func:`inspect` nor
:func:`commit` ever treats an existing-but-unreadable state as a mere
conflict: when at least one of the main and backup state files exists
but neither holds a valid state, :class:`CorruptStateError` propagates.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
import os
import re
from typing import Any

from . import audit as _audit
from . import receipt as _receipt
from . import storage as _storage

AUDIT = "audit"
ID = "id"
STAGE = "stage"
STATE = "state"
STATUS = "status"

ITEMS = "items"
VERSION = "version"

PREPARED = "prepared"
STAGE_STATE = "state"
STAGE_AUDIT = "audit"
COMMITTED = "committed"

_REQUEST_KEYS = (ID, STATE, AUDIT, STAGE)
_RESUME_KEYS = (ID, STATE, AUDIT)
_COMMIT_KEYS = (ID, STATE, "event")
_PATH_KEYS = ("checkpoint", STATE, AUDIT, "receipt")
_RECORD_KEYS = (AUDIT, ID, STAGE, STATE)
_INDEX_KEYS = (ITEMS, VERSION)
_INDEX_VERSION = 1

_EVENT = "event"
_CHECKPOINT = "checkpoint"
_RECEIPT = "receipt"

_STAGES = (PREPARED, STAGE_STATE, STAGE_AUDIT, COMMITTED)
_STAGE_RANK = {stage: rank for rank, stage in enumerate(_STAGES)}

# Statuses reported by inspect for a checkpoint against its artifacts.
RECOVERABLE = "recoverable"
CONFLICT = "conflict"

# Action performed once the checkpoint for a stage has been durably
# recorded: persist state after prepared, append the audit entry after
# state, bind the receipt after audit, and nothing after committed.
_NEXT_ACTIONS = {
    PREPARED: "persist_state",
    STAGE_STATE: "append_audit",
    STAGE_AUDIT: "bind_receipt",
    COMMITTED: "done",
}

_ID_RE = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}\Z")
_DIGEST_RE = re.compile(r"[0-9a-f]{64}\Z")


class CorruptTransactionError(ValueError):
    """The checkpoint index exists but its bytes are not a valid index."""


def _is_digest(value: Any) -> bool:
    return isinstance(value, str) and _DIGEST_RE.fullmatch(value) is not None


def _validated_request(request: Any) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Validate one checkpoint request and return a fresh dict in record order."""
    if not isinstance(request, dict):
        raise TypeError("request must be a dict")
    if set(request.keys()) != set(_REQUEST_KEYS):
        raise ValueError(
            "request must contain exactly the keys 'id', 'state', 'audit' "
            "and 'stage'"
        )
    for key in _REQUEST_KEYS:
        if not isinstance(request[key], str):
            raise TypeError(f"request {key} must be a str")
    checkpoint_id = request[ID]
    if _ID_RE.fullmatch(checkpoint_id) is None:
        raise ValueError("request id must match [A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}")
    if not _is_digest(request[STATE]):
        raise ValueError("request state must be 64 lowercase hex characters")
    if not _is_digest(request[AUDIT]):
        raise ValueError("request audit must be 64 lowercase hex characters")
    stage = request[STAGE]
    if stage not in _STAGE_RANK:
        raise ValueError(
            "request stage must be one of 'prepared', 'state', 'audit' or "
            "'committed'"
        )
    return {
        AUDIT: request[AUDIT],
        ID: checkpoint_id,
        STAGE: stage,
        STATE: request[STATE],
    }


def _validated_resume_request(request: Any) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Validate one resume request and return a fresh dict in record order."""
    if not isinstance(request, dict):
        raise TypeError("request must be a dict")
    if set(request.keys()) != set(_RESUME_KEYS):
        raise ValueError(
            "request must contain exactly the keys 'id', 'state' and 'audit'"
        )
    for key in _RESUME_KEYS:
        if not isinstance(request[key], str):
            raise TypeError(f"request {key} must be a str")
    checkpoint_id = request[ID]
    if _ID_RE.fullmatch(checkpoint_id) is None:
        raise ValueError("request id must match [A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}")
    if not _is_digest(request[STATE]):
        raise ValueError("request state must be 64 lowercase hex characters")
    if not _is_digest(request[AUDIT]):
        raise ValueError("request audit must be 64 lowercase hex characters")
    return {
        AUDIT: request[AUDIT],
        ID: checkpoint_id,
        STATE: request[STATE],
    }


def _serialize_index(records: list[dict[str, str]]) -> bytes:
    ordered = [
        {AUDIT: record[AUDIT], ID: record[ID], STAGE: record[STAGE],
         STATE: record[STATE]}
        for record in records
    ]
    index = {ITEMS: ordered, VERSION: _INDEX_VERSION}
    text = json.dumps(index, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":")) + "\n"
    return text.encode("utf-8")


def _parse_index(raw: bytes) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
    """Validate every byte of a checkpoint index and return its records.

    Raises :class:`CorruptTransactionError` for any UTF-8/JSON failure,
    non-canonical byte encoding, wrong key set, bad version, duplicate or
    unsorted ids, or a field that is not a well-formed str.  The order of
    object keys does not matter: a compact encoding whose only difference
    from the canonical form is key permutation is an equivalent index.
    """
    if raw == b"":
        raise CorruptTransactionError("checkpoint index is empty")
    try:
        text = raw.decode("utf-8")
    except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:
        raise CorruptTransactionError("checkpoint index is not valid UTF-8") from exc
    try:
        data = json.loads(text)
    except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
        raise CorruptTransactionError("checkpoint index is not valid JSON") from exc

    if not isinstance(data, dict):
        raise CorruptTransactionError("checkpoint index must be a JSON object")
    if set(data.keys()) != set(_INDEX_KEYS):
        raise CorruptTransactionError(
            "checkpoint index must contain exactly the keys 'items' and 'version'"
        )
    version = data[VERSION]
    # bool is a subclass of int; the version must be a genuine integer.
    if isinstance(version, bool) or not isinstance(version, int) or version != 1:
        raise CorruptTransactionError("checkpoint index version must be the integer 1")
    raw_items = data[ITEMS]
    if not isinstance(raw_items, list):
        raise CorruptTransactionError("checkpoint index items must be an array")

    records: list[dict[str, str]] = []
    for position, item in enumerate(raw_items):
        where = f"checkpoint index item {position}"
        if not isinstance(item, dict):
            raise CorruptTransactionError(f"{where} must be a JSON object")
        if set(item.keys()) != set(_RECORD_KEYS):
            raise CorruptTransactionError(
                f"{where} must contain exactly the keys 'audit', 'id', 'stage' "
                "and 'state'"
            )
        audit_digest = item[AUDIT]
        record_id = item[ID]
        stage = item[STAGE]
        state_digest = item[STATE]
        if not isinstance(record_id, str) or _ID_RE.fullmatch(record_id) is None:
            raise CorruptTransactionError(f"{where} has an invalid id")
        if not isinstance(stage, str) or stage not in _STAGE_RANK:
            raise CorruptTransactionError(f"{where} has an invalid stage")
        if not isinstance(state_digest, str) or not _is_digest(state_digest):
            raise CorruptTransactionError(
                f"{where} state must be 64 lowercase hex characters"
            )
        if not isinstance(audit_digest, str) or not _is_digest(audit_digest):
            raise CorruptTransactionError(
                f"{where} audit must be 64 lowercase hex characters"
            )
        records.append(
            {AUDIT: audit_digest, ID: record_id, STAGE: stage, STATE: state_digest}
        )

    ids = [record[ID] for record in records]
    if any(left >= right for left, right in zip(ids, ids[1:])):
        raise CorruptTransactionError(
            "checkpoint index ids must be unique and sorted ascending"
        )

    # Reject stray whitespace, non-canonical escapes, duplicate keys and
    # any encoding that is not a single compact form of the validated
    # structure.  Re-serialising the parsed object while preserving its
    # parsed key order tolerates permuted object keys (a semantically
    # equivalent compact index) while still rejecting every other
    # byte-level deviation; writes always use the canonical key order of
    # _serialize_index.
    if not raw.endswith(b"\n") or raw.endswith(b"\n\n"):
        raise CorruptTransactionError(
            "checkpoint index must end with exactly one newline"
        )
    compact = json.dumps(data, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"))
    if compact != text[:-1]:
        raise CorruptTransactionError("checkpoint index is not canonically encoded")
    return records


def _read_index(path: str) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
    try:
        with open(path, "rb") as handle:
            raw = handle.read()
    except FileNotFoundError:
        return []
    return _parse_index(raw)


def _atomic_write(path: str, payload: bytes) -> None:
    tmp_path = path + ".tmp"
    with open(tmp_path, "wb") as handle:
        handle.write(payload)
        handle.flush()
        os.fsync(handle.fileno())
    try:
        os.replace(tmp_path, path)
    except BaseException:
        try:
            os.unlink(tmp_path)
        except OSError:
            pass
        raise
    fd = os.open(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(path)), os.O_RDONLY)
    try:
        os.fsync(fd)
    finally:
        os.close(fd)


def _apply(
    path: str, records: list[dict[str, str]], record: dict[str, str]
) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
    """Apply ``record`` to ``records`` and return the resulting record list."""
    for position, existing in enumerate(records):
        if existing[ID] != record[ID]:
            continue
        if (
            existing[STATE] != record[STATE]
            or existing[AUDIT] != record[AUDIT]
        ):
            raise ValueError(
                f"checkpoint id {record[ID]!r} is already bound to different "
                "state or audit digests"
            )
        old_rank = _STAGE_RANK[existing[STAGE]]
        new_rank = _STAGE_RANK[record[STAGE]]
        if new_rank == old_rank:
            # Idempotent replay: no filesystem change.
            return records
        if new_rank < old_rank:
            raise ValueError(
                f"checkpoint id {record[ID]!r} cannot regress from stage "
                f"{existing[STAGE]!r} to {record[STAGE]!r}"
            )
        if new_rank > old_rank + 1:
            raise ValueError(
                f"checkpoint id {record[ID]!r} cannot skip from stage "
                f"{existing[STAGE]!r} to {record[STAGE]!r}"
            )
        updated = list(records)
        updated[position] = record
        _atomic_write(path, _serialize_index(updated))
        return updated

    if record[STAGE] != PREPARED:
        raise ValueError("a new checkpoint id must start at the 'prepared' stage")
    updated = sorted(records + [record], key=lambda entry: entry[ID])
    _atomic_write(path, _serialize_index(updated))
    return updated


def checkpoint(
    path: str, request: dict[str, str] | None = None
) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
    """Record or query a replayable commit checkpoint at ``path``.

    With ``request=None`` this is a pure query returning every checkpoint.
    Otherwise ``request`` must contain exactly the str keys ``id``,
    ``state``, ``audit`` and ``stage``: ``id`` matches
    ``[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}``, ``state`` and ``audit`` are 64 lowercase hex
    characters, and ``stage`` is one of ``prepared``, ``state``, ``audit``
    or ``committed``.

    A new id is inserted at ``prepared``; an existing id with identical
    digests replays idempotently at the same stage or advances one adjacent
    stage.  Changed digests, a stage regression or a skipped stage raise
    :class:`ValueError` and leave the file unchanged.  In every case a
    brand-new list sorted ascending by ``id`` is returned, each element a
    fresh dict with the key order ``audit``, ``id``, ``stage``, ``state``.

    Type violations raise :class:`TypeError`; a bad key set, field format
    or stage migration raises :class:`ValueError`; a corrupt index raises
    :class:`CorruptTransactionError`; other filesystem errors propagate as
    :class:`OSError`.
    """
    if not isinstance(path, str):
        raise TypeError("path must be a str")

    record = _validated_request(request) if request is not None else None
    records = _read_index(path)
    if record is not None:
        records = _apply(path, records, record)

    return [
        {
            AUDIT: record[AUDIT],
            ID: record[ID],
            STAGE: record[STAGE],
            STATE: record[STATE],
        }
        for record in records
    ]


def resume(
    path: str, request: dict[str, str], observed: str | None = None
) -> str:
    """Recover one commit step at ``path`` and return the next action.

    ``request`` must contain exactly the str keys ``id``, ``state`` and
    ``audit`` in the same format as the matching :func:`checkpoint`
    fields.  ``observed`` must be ``None`` or one of the stages
    ``prepared``, ``state``, ``audit`` or ``committed``; it names the
    stage the caller has observed for the id.

    A new id is only accepted with ``observed=None`` and is recorded at
    the ``prepared`` stage.  An existing id must be bound to the same
    ``state`` and ``audit`` digests; with ``observed=None`` or the
    current stage the call is a pure query and leaves the file bytes
    untouched, while ``observed`` naming the adjacent next stage
    advances the checkpoint exactly once.  A stage regression, a skipped
    stage or an illegal ``observed`` value raise :class:`ValueError` and
    leave the file unchanged.

    The return value is the next action for the processed stage:
    ``persist_state`` for ``prepared``, ``append_audit`` for ``state``,
    ``bind_receipt`` for ``audit`` and ``done`` for ``committed``.

    A non-str ``observed`` other than ``None`` raises :class:`TypeError`;
    the remaining type and value rules, :class:`CorruptTransactionError`
    and :class:`OSError` propagation match :func:`checkpoint`.
    """
    if not isinstance(path, str):
        raise TypeError("path must be a str")

    requested = _validated_resume_request(request)
    if observed is not None:
        if not isinstance(observed, str):
            raise TypeError(
                "observed must be None or one of 'prepared', 'state', "
                "'audit' or 'committed'"
            )
        if observed not in _STAGE_RANK:
            raise ValueError(
                "observed must be None or one of 'prepared', 'state', "
                "'audit' or 'committed'"
            )

    records = _read_index(path)
    existing = next(
        (record for record in records if record[ID] == requested[ID]), None
    )

    if existing is None:
        if observed is not None:
            raise ValueError(
                f"checkpoint id {requested[ID]!r} is new and may only be "
                "resumed with observed=None"
            )
        record = {
            AUDIT: requested[AUDIT],
            ID: requested[ID],
            STAGE: PREPARED,
            STATE: requested[STATE],
        }
        _apply(path, records, record)
        return _NEXT_ACTIONS[PREPARED]

    if (
        existing[STATE] != requested[STATE]
        or existing[AUDIT] != requested[AUDIT]
    ):
        raise ValueError(
            f"checkpoint id {requested[ID]!r} is already bound to different "
            "state or audit digests"
        )

    current_stage = existing[STAGE]
    if observed is None or observed == current_stage:
        # Pure query: no filesystem change.
        processed_stage = current_stage
    else:
        current_rank = _STAGE_RANK[current_stage]
        observed_rank = _STAGE_RANK[observed]
        if observed_rank < current_rank:
            raise ValueError(
                f"checkpoint id {requested[ID]!r} cannot regress from stage "
                f"{current_stage!r} to {observed!r}"
            )
        if observed_rank > current_rank + 1:
            raise ValueError(
                f"checkpoint id {requested[ID]!r} cannot skip from stage "
                f"{current_stage!r} to {observed!r}"
            )
        record = {
            AUDIT: requested[AUDIT],
            ID: requested[ID],
            STAGE: observed,
            STATE: requested[STATE],
        }
        _apply(path, records, record)
        processed_stage = observed

    return _NEXT_ACTIONS[processed_stage]



def _state_payload(state: dict[str, Any]) -> bytes:
    """The canonical storage bytes for a validated merge state."""
    clock, records = _storage._validated_state(state)
    return _storage._serialize(clock, records)


def _validated_paths(paths: Any) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Validate the ``checkpoint``/``state``/``audit``/``receipt`` path map."""
    if not isinstance(paths, dict):
        raise TypeError("paths must be a dict")
    if set(paths.keys()) != set(_PATH_KEYS):
        raise ValueError(
            "paths must contain exactly the keys 'checkpoint', 'state', "
            "'audit' and 'receipt'"
        )
    for key in _PATH_KEYS:
        if not isinstance(paths[key], str):
            raise TypeError(f"paths {key} must be a str")
    return {key: paths[key] for key in _PATH_KEYS}


def _validated_commit_inputs(
    paths: Any, request: Any
) -> tuple[dict[str, str], str, dict[str, Any], dict[str, str], bytes]:
    """Validate ``paths`` and a commit ``request`` before any file access.

    Returns the path map, id, the caller's state, a fresh validated event
    dict and the canonical state bytes.  The state is checked against the
    merge state contract and the event against the audit event contract,
    so their type/value errors propagate unchanged in kind.
    """
    path_map = _validated_paths(paths)
    if not isinstance(request, dict):
        raise TypeError("request must be a dict")
    if set(request.keys()) != set(_COMMIT_KEYS):
        raise ValueError(
            "request must contain exactly the keys 'id', 'state' and 'event'"
        )
    checkpoint_id = request[ID]
    if not isinstance(checkpoint_id, str):
        raise TypeError("request id must be a str")
    if _ID_RE.fullmatch(checkpoint_id) is None:
        raise ValueError("request id must match [A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}")

    payload = _state_payload(request[STATE])
    event = _audit._validated_event(request[_EVENT])

    return path_map, checkpoint_id, request[STATE], event, payload


def _planned_audit_digest(
    audit_records: list[dict[str, Any]], event: dict[str, str]
) -> str:
    """Hash the audit record the next :func:`audit.append` would write.

    Deterministic from the log's current tail: its seq is one past the
    last record and its prev is the last record's hash (or the zero hash
    for an empty log).
    """
    seq = len(audit_records) + 1
    prev = audit_records[-1][_audit.HASH] if audit_records else _audit._ZERO_HASH
    without_hash = {
        _audit.DETAIL: event[_audit.DETAIL],
        _audit.KIND: event[_audit.KIND],
        _audit.PREV: prev,
        _audit.SEQ: seq,
        _audit.SOURCE: event[_audit.SOURCE],
    }
    return _audit._record_hash(without_hash)


def _event_matches(record: dict[str, Any], event: dict[str, str]) -> bool:
    return (
        record[_audit.SOURCE] == event[_audit.SOURCE]
        and record[_audit.KIND] == event[_audit.KIND]
        and record[_audit.DETAIL] == event[_audit.DETAIL]
    )


def _advance(
    path: str,
    records: list[dict[str, str]],
    checkpoint_id: str,
    state_digest: str,
    audit_digest: str,
    stage: str,
) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
    """Advance (or insert at ``prepared``) the checkpoint for one stage."""
    record = {
        AUDIT: audit_digest,
        ID: checkpoint_id,
        STAGE: stage,
        STATE: state_digest,
    }
    return _apply(path, records, record)


def _main_state_canonical_bytes(path: str) -> bytes | None:
    """Canonical complete bytes of the main state file, or ``None``.

    Only the main file is consulted: ``None`` is returned when it is
    missing or when its bytes do not decode to a valid state.  No
    exception other than a non-:class:`FileNotFoundError`
    :class:`OSError` escapes.
    """
    try:
        with open(path, "rb") as handle:
            raw = handle.read()
    except FileNotFoundError:
        return None
    try:
        state = _storage._decode_state(raw)
    except _storage._DECODE_FAILURES:
        return None
    return _state_payload(state)


def _read_state_bytes(path: str) -> bytes | None:
    """Return the raw main state file bytes, or None when it is absent.

    Every :class:`OSError` other than :class:`FileNotFoundError`
    propagates unchanged.
    """
    try:
        with open(path, "rb") as handle:
            return handle.read()
    except FileNotFoundError:
        return None


def _assert_state_loadable(path: str) -> None:
    """Raise unless the state is absent or a valid state survives.

    Mirrors :func:`storage.load_state`: when at least one of the main and
    backup files exists but neither holds a valid state,
    :class:`CorruptStateError` propagates unchanged; when neither file
    exists nothing happens.  Every other :class:`OSError` propagates
    unchanged as well.
    """
    try:
        _storage.load_state(path)
    except FileNotFoundError:
        return


def _inspect_status(
    stage: str,
    state_matches: bool,
    audit_ok: bool,
    receipt: dict[str, str] | None,
    state_digest: str,
    audit_digest: str,
) -> str:
    """Classify one checkpoint from its stage and the S/A/R0/R1 facts.

    ``S`` is ``state_matches`` (the main state file's canonical bytes hash
    to the state digest), ``A`` is ``audit_ok`` (a valid audit chain
    carries the audit digest), ``R0`` means no receipt is bound under the
    id and ``R1`` means that receipt binds exactly both digests.
    ``prepared`` with ``not A and R0``, ``state`` with ``S and R0`` and
    ``audit`` with ``S and A and (R0 or R1)`` are recoverable;
    ``committed`` with ``S and A and R1`` is committed; everything else
    is a conflict.
    """
    r0 = receipt is None
    r1 = (
        receipt is not None
        and receipt[STATE] == state_digest
        and receipt[AUDIT] == audit_digest
    )
    if stage == PREPARED:
        if not audit_ok and r0:
            return RECOVERABLE
    elif stage == STAGE_STATE:
        if state_matches and r0:
            return RECOVERABLE
    elif stage == STAGE_AUDIT:
        if state_matches and audit_ok and (r0 or r1):
            return RECOVERABLE
    else:  # COMMITTED
        if state_matches and audit_ok and r1:
            return COMMITTED
    return CONFLICT


def inspect(paths: dict[str, str]) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
    """Read-only inspection of every checkpoint against its bound artifacts.

    ``paths`` must contain exactly the str keys ``checkpoint``, ``state``,
    ``audit`` and ``receipt``, naming the checkpoint index, the main state
    file (its ``path + ".bak"`` backup is consulted for corruption
    detection, exactly as :func:`storage.load_state` does), the audit log
    and the receipt index.

    A missing checkpoint index yields ``[]`` (no other artifact is read in
    that case).  Otherwise one fresh dict per checkpoint is returned sorted
    ascending by ``id`` with the fixed key order ``audit``, ``id``,
    ``stage``, ``state``, ``status``; the first four values are copied from
    the checkpoint and ``status`` is one of ``recoverable``, ``committed``
    or ``conflict``.

    Let ``S`` mean the main state file holds a complete valid state whose
    canonical bytes hash to the state digest, ``A`` mean a valid audit
    chain contains a record whose hash is the audit digest, ``R0`` mean no
    receipt is bound under the id and ``R1`` mean that receipt binds
    exactly both digests.  A ``prepared`` checkpoint with ``not A and R0``,
    a ``state`` checkpoint with ``S and R0`` and an ``audit`` checkpoint
    with ``S and A and (R0 or R1)`` are ``recoverable``; a ``committed``
    checkpoint with ``S and A and R1`` is ``committed``; every other
    combination is ``conflict``.

    No file is created or modified.  Type violations raise
    :class:`TypeError` and a bad path key set raises :class:`ValueError`;
    when at least one of the state main/backup files exists but neither
    holds a valid state, :class:`CorruptStateError` propagates unchanged,
    as do :class:`CorruptAuditError`, :class:`CorruptReceiptError`,
    :class:`CorruptTransactionError` and :class:`OSError`.
    """
    path_map = _validated_paths(paths)

    records = _read_index(path_map[_CHECKPOINT])
    if not records:
        return []

    audit_records = _audit._read_all_records(path_map[AUDIT])
    receipts_by_id = {
        receipt[ID]: receipt for receipt in _receipt._read_index(path_map[_RECEIPT])
    }
    main_state_bytes = _main_state_canonical_bytes(path_map[STATE])
    _assert_state_loadable(path_map[STATE])

    audit_hashes = {record[_audit.HASH] for record in audit_records}

    items: list[dict[str, str]] = []
    for record in records:
        state_digest = record[STATE]
        audit_digest = record[AUDIT]
        state_matches = (
            main_state_bytes is not None
            and hashlib.sha256(main_state_bytes).hexdigest() == state_digest
        )
        audit_ok = audit_digest in audit_hashes
        receipt = receipts_by_id.get(record[ID])
        status = _inspect_status(
            record[STAGE], state_matches, audit_ok, receipt,
            state_digest, audit_digest,
        )
        items.append(
            {
                AUDIT: audit_digest,
                ID: record[ID],
                STAGE: record[STAGE],
                STATE: state_digest,
                STATUS: status,
            }
        )
    return items


def commit(paths: dict[str, str], request: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Run one replayable commit across storage, audit, receipt and checkpoint.

    ``paths`` must contain exactly the str keys ``checkpoint``, ``state``,
    ``audit`` and ``receipt``.  ``request`` must contain exactly the keys
    ``id`` (same format as :func:`checkpoint`), ``state`` (a state obeying
    the :mod:`~offline_coordination.merge` state contract) and ``event``
    (an event obeying the :mod:`~offline_coordination.audit` event
    contract).

    The state digest is the lowercase-hex SHA-256 of the complete
    canonical state bytes (including the trailing ``\\n``) that
    :mod:`~offline_coordination.storage` persists; the audit digest is
    the hash of the single audit record appended for this commit.  A
    first commit saves the state, appends exactly one audit event, binds
    a receipt carrying the id and both digests, and advances the
    checkpoint through ``prepared``, ``state``, ``audit`` and
    ``committed`` in that order.

    Replaying the same arguments -- or re-entering after an interruption
    -- resumes at the recorded stage and performs each remaining side
    effect at most once, so the result is identical and no effect is
    duplicated.  Every artifact is reconciled against the checkpoint
    stage before any file is touched: a digest conflict, or a stage
    whose state file, audit record or receipt is missing, extra or
    mismatched, raises :class:`ValueError` and leaves the files
    unchanged.

    On success a brand-new dict is returned with the key order
    ``audit``, ``id``, ``stage``, ``state`` and ``stage`` equal to
    ``committed``.  Type violations raise :class:`TypeError`; bad key
    sets, formats, state/event values, digest conflicts and stage/
    artifact mismatches raise :class:`ValueError`;
    :class:`CorruptStateError`, :class:`CorruptAuditError`,
    :class:`CorruptReceiptError`, :class:`CorruptTransactionError` and
    :class:`OSError` propagate unchanged.
    """
    (
        path_map,
        checkpoint_id,
        state,
        event,
        payload,
    ) = _validated_commit_inputs(paths, request)
    checkpoint_path = path_map[_CHECKPOINT]
    state_path = path_map[STATE]
    audit_path = path_map[AUDIT]
    receipt_path = path_map[_RECEIPT]

    state_digest = hashlib.sha256(payload).hexdigest()

    # Read every artifact up front.  All reconciliation below happens
    # before any mutation, so a rejected commit changes nothing.
    audit_records = _audit._read_all_records(audit_path)
    planned_audit_digest = _planned_audit_digest(audit_records, event)
    bound_receipt = _receipt.get(receipt_path, checkpoint_id)
    records = _read_index(checkpoint_path)
    existing = next(
        (record for record in records if record[ID] == checkpoint_id), None
    )
    state_on_disk = _read_state_bytes(state_path)
    # When a state file exists but neither the main file nor the backup
    # holds a valid state the situation is unrecoverable, not a digest
    # conflict: CorruptStateError propagates before any reconciliation.
    _assert_state_loadable(state_path)

    need_save = False
    need_append = False
    need_receipt = False

    if existing is None:
        # An id absent from the checkpoint index cannot have produced any
        # artifact of its own yet; a receipt bound under it is a conflict.
        if bound_receipt is not None:
            raise ValueError(
                f"receipt id {checkpoint_id!r} is already bound but no "
                "checkpoint exists for it"
            )
        audit_digest = planned_audit_digest
        stage = PREPARED
        # The state save is the first artifact effect; it is pending
        # unless the main file already holds the committed bytes.
        need_save = state_on_disk != payload
        need_append = True
        need_receipt = True
    else:
        if existing[STATE] != state_digest:
            raise ValueError(
                f"checkpoint id {checkpoint_id!r} is already bound to a "
                "different state digest"
            )
        audit_digest = existing[AUDIT]
        stage = existing[STAGE]
        audit_record = next(
            (item for item in audit_records
             if item[_audit.HASH] == audit_digest),
            None,
        )

        if stage == PREPARED:
            # The event has not been appended yet, so its record hash must
            # still be derivable from the current log tail.
            if audit_digest != planned_audit_digest:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"checkpoint id {checkpoint_id!r} is already bound to a "
                    "different audit digest"
                )
            if audit_record is not None:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"checkpoint id {checkpoint_id!r} is at stage 'prepared' "
                    "but its audit record is already present"
                )
            if bound_receipt is not None:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"checkpoint id {checkpoint_id!r} is at stage 'prepared' "
                    "but a receipt is already bound"
                )
            # The save is pending unless the main file already holds the
            # committed bytes; save_state itself rotates any prior state.
            need_save = state_on_disk != payload
            need_append = True
            need_receipt = True
        elif stage == STAGE_STATE:
            if state_on_disk != payload:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"checkpoint id {checkpoint_id!r} is past stage "
                    "'prepared' but its state file is missing or mismatched"
                )
            if bound_receipt is not None:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"checkpoint id {checkpoint_id!r} is at stage 'state' but "
                    "a receipt is already bound"
                )
            if audit_record is None:
                # The append may still be pending; the log tail must still
                # derive the bound record for this event.
                if audit_digest != planned_audit_digest:
                    raise ValueError(
                        f"checkpoint id {checkpoint_id!r} is at stage 'state' "
                        "but its audit record is missing"
                    )
                need_append = True
            elif not _event_matches(audit_record, event):
                raise ValueError(
                    f"checkpoint id {checkpoint_id!r} audit record does not "
                    "match its committed event"
                )
            need_receipt = True
        elif stage == STAGE_AUDIT:
            if state_on_disk != payload:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"checkpoint id {checkpoint_id!r} is past stage "
                    "'prepared' but its state file is missing or mismatched"
                )
            if audit_record is None:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"checkpoint id {checkpoint_id!r} is past stage 'state' "
                    "but its audit record is missing"
                )
            if not _event_matches(audit_record, event):
                raise ValueError(
                    f"checkpoint id {checkpoint_id!r} audit record does not "
                    "match its committed event"
                )
            if bound_receipt is None:
                need_receipt = True
            elif (
                bound_receipt[STATE] != state_digest
                or bound_receipt[AUDIT] != audit_digest
            ):
                raise ValueError(
                    f"checkpoint id {checkpoint_id!r} receipt is bound to "
                    "different state or audit digests"
                )
        else:  # COMMITTED
            if state_on_disk != payload:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"checkpoint id {checkpoint_id!r} is past stage "
                    "'prepared' but its state file is missing or mismatched"
                )
            if audit_record is None:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"checkpoint id {checkpoint_id!r} is past stage 'state' "
                    "but its audit record is missing"
                )
            if not _event_matches(audit_record, event):
                raise ValueError(
                    f"checkpoint id {checkpoint_id!r} audit record does not "
                    "match its committed event"
                )
            if bound_receipt is None:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"checkpoint id {checkpoint_id!r} is committed but its "
                    "receipt is missing"
                )
            if (
                bound_receipt[STATE] != state_digest
                or bound_receipt[AUDIT] != audit_digest
            ):
                raise ValueError(
                    f"checkpoint id {checkpoint_id!r} receipt is bound to "
                    "different state or audit digests"
                )

    # Reconciliation succeeded; perform each remaining effect at most
    # once and advance the checkpoint after every durable step.
    if existing is None:
        records = _advance(
            checkpoint_path, records, checkpoint_id,
            state_digest, audit_digest, PREPARED,
        )

    if stage == PREPARED:
        if need_save:
            _storage.save_state(state_path, state)
        records = _advance(
            checkpoint_path, records, checkpoint_id,
            state_digest, audit_digest, STAGE_STATE,
        )
        stage = STAGE_STATE

    if stage == STAGE_STATE:
        if need_append:
            _audit.append(audit_path, event)
        records = _advance(
            checkpoint_path, records, checkpoint_id,
            state_digest, audit_digest, STAGE_AUDIT,
        )
        stage = STAGE_AUDIT

    if stage == STAGE_AUDIT:
        if need_receipt:
            _receipt.put(
                receipt_path,
                {AUDIT: audit_digest, ID: checkpoint_id, STATE: state_digest},
            )
        _advance(
            checkpoint_path, records, checkpoint_id,
            state_digest, audit_digest, COMMITTED,
        )

    return {
        AUDIT: audit_digest,
        ID: checkpoint_id,
        STAGE: COMMITTED,
        STATE: state_digest,
    }

136	``null`` when those ``before`` digests differ.  ``conflictSeq`` is
137	``null`` for every non-fork relation.  The bytes are deterministic for
138	equal inputs; swapping the inputs only exchanges ``left``/``right`` and
139	mirrors the prefix direction.
140	
141	:func:`plan_merge` turns that read-only comparison into a read-only merge
142	plan.  It takes both proof byte strings and a conflict ``policy`` --
143	``"left"``, ``"right"`` or ``"manual"``; any other value raises
144	:class:`ValueError` -- and validates every argument type before parsing
145	either proof, so a malformed proof never masks a :class:`TypeError` and an
146	invalid proof still raises :class:`InvalidProofError`.  Disjoint ranges,
147	or a fork whose common boundary cannot be confirmed, raise
148	:class:`ValueError` instead of producing a speculative plan.  Only
149	complete entries strictly after the common boundary become steps: an
150	unforked history accepts the longer side's tail as an ``extension``; a
151	fork accepts the selected side's tail (``selected``) and rejects the
152	other (``rejected``), while ``manual`` marks both tails ``manual`` and
153	references them from ``unresolved``.  The plan is one version-1 UTF-8
154	compact JSON object -- keys recursively sorted, non-ASCII preserved,
155	exactly one trailing ``\\n`` -- with the top-level keys ``common``,
156	``left``, ``policy``, ``relation``, ``right``, ``steps``, ``unresolved``
157	and ``version``; steps carry the original entries unchanged and are
158	ordered by ascending seq with the left side first on ties.  The plan is
159	byte-stable for equal inputs, mirrors left/right when the proofs are
160	swapped together with a ``left``/``right`` policy, and never touches the
161	filesystem or the inputs.
162	
163	:func:`resolve_merge` closes a ``manual`` plan read-only.  It takes the
164	plan byte string, the same two proofs and a list of decisions; only a
165	``manual`` plan produced by :func:`plan_merge` for exactly those proofs
166	may be resolved -- a plan from any other policy is a structurally valid
167	version-1 plan whose steps differ from the regenerated manual plan and
168	is therefore rejected as stale before any decision is considered.
169	A structurally invalid plan (encoding, duplicate keys, version-1
170	structure) raises :class:`InvalidPlanError`; a structurally valid plan
171	that is not byte-for-byte the manual plan regenerated from the proofs
172	(digest, relation, common boundary, side summaries, steps or unresolved
173	references) raises :class:`StalePlanError`; both are
174	:class:`ValueError` subclasses.  Each decision carries only ``side``,
175	``seq`` and ``action`` (``"accept"`` or ``"reject"``), resolving one
176	unresolved reference; missing, duplicate, extra or out-of-range
177	references and illegal choices raise :class:`InvalidResolutionError`
178	(a :class:`ValueError`).  Accepted entries must chain contiguously from
179	the common boundary -- at most one accepted side per seq, no acceptance
180	past a rejected seq, an unbroken seq and digest chain.  The result is
181	one version-1 compact JSON object with the top-level keys ``common``,
182	``left``, ``planDigest``, ``relation``, ``right``, ``steps``,
183	``unresolved`` and ``version``; manual steps become
184	``accept``/``reject`` with the fixed reasons ``manual-accepted``/
185	``manual-rejected``, non-manual steps, carried audit entries and ``auth``
186	bindings are unchanged, ``unresolved`` is empty and ``planDigest`` is the
187	lowercase hex SHA-256 of the complete source plan bytes.  Resolution is
188	deterministic, mirrors under a left/right swap with matching decisions,
189	and never touches the filesystem or the inputs.
190	
191	:func:`commit_resolution` is the write entry point that lands a manual
192	resolution in the ledger.  It takes the ledger path, the canonical
193	resolution bytes, the original plan bytes, both proofs and the landing
194	material -- the final ``state`` plus ``requests`` binding every accepted
195	entry id to its request digest.  Both proofs are verified offline and
196	the plan and resolution are checked against the freshly regenerated
197	manual plan (:class:`StalePlanError` otherwise, without touching the
198	ledger); the ledger itself must still sit at the resolution's common
199	boundary (:class:`StaleLedgerError`, a :class:`ValueError`).  A fully
200	identical replay is recognized before that staleness check and returns
201	``duplicate``; a resolution accepting nothing returns ``unchanged`` and
202	writes nothing.  Otherwise the final state, the request bindings and
203	the contiguous accepted entries -- rejected entries never enter the
204	audit -- are written in one fail-safe replacement, returning
205	``applied``.  The result carries only ``next``, ``resolutionDigest``
206	and ``status``.
207	"""
